The complement of a closed cap is convex, so every captured image point has a captured endpoint. Multiplying the two normalized endpoint probabilities by min(A,B) bounds each by its original side measure.
Adding the entire central measure gives W=M−max(A,B); if one side is zero, the same identity follows directly from the central measure. The median inequalities give W≥M/2 in either case.

Integrating the actual pointwise finite weighted cover against the target gives the exact W lower bound for arbitrary nonnegative weights. Source ddedecc7f627090b gives the same target and weighted bound.
